city_center.name: Downtown Omaha / Old Market
city_center.landmark: The Old Market -- a brick-and-cobblestone warehouse district on the Missouri River bluff; the river and Bob Kerrey pedestrian bridge anchor the riverfront
city_center.notes: Omaha grew as a Missouri River gateway and railroad-and-livestock city; the Old Market is a preserved brick warehouse district with cobblestone streets. Omaha's grocery market is split roughly evenly between Walmart, Hy-Vee, and Baker's (a Kroger banner). sources: Omaha grocery market share Walmart / Hy-Vee / Baker's (supermarketnews.com Omaha upscale market share); Hy-Vee Nebraska ranking (supermarketnews.com Kroger-Hy-Vee Midwest).

cultural_notes: Omaha grew as a Missouri River gateway and a railroad-and-livestock city; the Old Market is a preserved brick-and-cobblestone warehouse district that defines the downtown texture (INFERRED architectural framing from region knowledge -- verify specific claims before production)

Omaha's grocery market share is split nearly evenly among Walmart, Hy-Vee, and Baker's / Dillon (a Kroger subsidiary) -- no single dominant grocer, unlike the Texas H-E-B or Iowa Hy-Vee monopolies (source: supermarketnews.com Operators Seek More of Omaha's Upscale Market Share)

Hy-Vee is an employee-owned midwest chain that ranks first in visits in Nebraska in some measures and captured ~41% of Nebraska grocery visits in one monthly report -- a strong but not exclusive regional loyalty (source: supermarketnews.com Kroger-Hy-Vee Midwest; supermarketnews.com Kroger-Hy-Vee January visits)

South Omaha holds a large Hispanic community rooted in the old stockyards / meatpacking labor history -- creative should read heartland-multicultural, not single-heritage (INFERRED framing -- verify before production use)
